meeting_header: Attendees (Redwood): Avery Chen, Marcus Lane, Priya Nair
Attendees (Customer): Daniel Ortiz, Rina Patel, Samir Kapoor, Elena Gomez
summary: Kickoff for activation/pilot of Redwood inference for QuarryBay's route-optimization and shipment tagging workloads. Focus on networking options (VPC vs hosted private), latency SLOs, and security/compliance items. Agreed to run bench tests and share security artifacts; pilot target early November.
topics: Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
transcript: [00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we're gonna run about 50 minutes, lots to get through, quick intros?
[00:12] Daniel Ortiz: Hi yes Daniel here, CTO, excited to see how Redwood can help our real-time routing, we've been struggling with tail latencies
[00:22] Rina Patel: Rina, platform eng. We'll own integration work. Our infra is mostly Kubernetes on a managed cloud and we have on-prem edge boxes in EU.
[00:38] Priya Nair: Priya from CS, I'll be your onboarding lead and help with runbook and cutover planning, hi all
[00:46] Marcus Lane: Marcus SE, I'll lead the performance benching and help with model choices and quantization recommendations
[00:55] Elena Gomez: Elena program manager, I'll coordinate stakeholders and timelines — thanks for meeting
[01:05] Avery Chen: Great. Quick agenda: 1) current stack and constraints 2) deployment options and security needs 3) pilot scope and metrics 4) next steps. Sound ok?

[01:18] Daniel Ortiz: Yep sounds good. I'll start with a bit of background — QuarryBay runs route optimization service that enriches shipments with LLM-generated intent tags and routing notes, this is on critical path for our carrier assignment logic

[01:36] Rina Patel: To add, we've got peaks during end-of-day batch windows with spiky qps. Typical p95 target is 150ms across the stack, but LLMs today blow that up so we want 99th percentile under 300ms for the inference piece
[01:54] Samir Kapoor: From security — we need data residency in EU for certain customers, also we must integrate with our KMS and audit logs; SOC2 is required, and SSO via SAML is a must

[02:10] Marcus Lane: Noted. There are multiple knobs — model selection, quantization, batching, and routing. On Hosted API you get fast time-to-value but less control over residency; Dedicated gives committed capacity and better tail control; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives residency and KMS integration. We can sketch tradeoffs
[02:34] Rina Patel: For us, residency + KMS + ability to pin model version are critical. We might accept slightly higher cost for guaranteed p99 though pricing will matter
[02:48] Daniel Ortiz: Also curious about graceful degradation — if the model cluster is under pressure can we fallback to a cheaper smaller model with same schema?

[02:58] Marcus Lane: Yes we have smart routing and fallback policies — you can specify model variants, cascade to lower-cost quantized models. The runtime also supports prefix caching and KV cache to reduce repeated token costs, though spelled out in docs it's sometimes written as kv cash in the old exports haha
[03:18] Priya Nair: Could you briefly describe the console observability? Our ops wants token-level cost and latency per route
[03:28] Avery Chen: Redwood Console gives per-route dashboards, token breakdown, tracing hooks, and alerts. We can share screenshots and a short demo during pilot handoff
[03:39] Elena Gomez: Timeline — we want pilot in the first half of November. Stakeholders include platform, security, and SRE. Can we make that happen?
[03:50] Marcus Lane: It's tight but doable. Two parallel tasks: security artifacts and bench runs. We'll need Rina's traffic profile and sample prompts to reproduce realistic latencies
[04:04] Rina Patel: I'll share qps patterns and a sanitized prompt set. We have spikes up to 800 qps at peak, 99th currently blows to ~800ms in our probe cluster
[04:16] Samir Kapoor: On compliance, we need to see Redwood's SOC2 and proof of encryption at rest + KMS integration, also audit log retention policies — can you send that today or tomorrow?
[04:26] Avery Chen: Yes, I'll send our security pack and KMS integration notes by Friday. For audit logs we support configurable retention and we can integrate with your SIEM via delivery hooks
[04:39] Daniel Ortiz: Regarding network — we prefer VPC peering or Private Link into our cloud region. On-prem at the edge might be an opt-in for a future phase
[04:52] Marcus Lane: We support VPC-based Private deployments and on-prem packages for air-gapped. For the pilot we usually do Dedicated in a region with VPC peering to mimic production latency
[05:05] Elena Gomez: Cost question — what's the typical unit economics and does batching hurt p95?

[05:12] Marcus Lane: Batching is workload-aware; it improves throughput but can increase single-request latency if you set a larger batch window. We can recommend configs to meet your p99 and reduce tokens cost via caching and quantization. Redwood Optimize will surface recommended batch sizes
[05:28] Rina Patel: Any constraints on model sizes for Dedicated? We're evaluating a 13B and a 70B variant depending on quality tradeoffs

[05:37] Marcus Lane: Dedicated supports a range of model sizes; the runtime chooses kernels and quantization path. For 70B you get better quality but cost and tail latency risk — we can suggest 4-bit quant with warmed KV cache for most traffic
[05:52] Samir Kapoor: How is the KV cache secured? If cache keys include customer IDs we need encryption and access controls

[05:59] Marcus Lane: KV cache keys are kept in-memory on GPU hosts; for Private deployments keys never leave your VPC and we can document encryption-at-rest for persisted shards and RBAC on control plane

[06:12] Daniel Ortiz: For pilot success criteria: 1) p99 inference <= 300ms on pilot traffic, 2) clear path to EU residency, 3) security checklist satisfied. If all green, we'll talk committed Dedicated capacity
[06:28] Avery Chen: Good crisp criteria. We'll aim to deliver a bench report with p50/p95/p99 and tail latency histograms and include configuration we used
[06:38] Elena Gomez: Who will be the primary tech POC during benching?
[06:42] Rina Patel: That'll be me — I'll coordinate sample payloads and access to test harness
[06:48] Marcus Lane: Awesome. Also can you confirm whether you need data residency for embeddings or just inference outputs? Sometimes embeddings have different residency rules
[06:58] Samir Kapoor: We need residency for customer PII and embeddings derived from PII; ephemeral inference of public metadata is ok in US but we'd prefer EU for the pilot to be safe
[07:10] Avery Chen: Noted — we'll treat embeddings as sensitive and plan for Private/VPC-based pilot in EU region if that's what you prefer
[07:22] Daniel Ortiz: Onboarding tasks — do you provide Terraform modules or helm charts for Dedicated/Private?
[07:30] Marcus Lane: Yes we have reusable terraform modules for VPC networking and helm charts for the on-prem operator. For Dedicated there's a simple peering guide. We'll share links
[07:40] Elena Gomez: Ok good. About SSO: we need SAML integration for SRE and RBAC roles mapped to our groups
[07:49] Priya Nair: We support SAML and SCIM for group sync; we'll work with Samir on role mappings and Priya (CSM) will run the SSO test
[08:00] Samir Kapoor: Also we have an internal procurement step: legal will need an addendum for data residency and DPA. Can you surface sample contracts?
[08:09] Avery Chen: I'll queue up our DPA and sample Dedicated terms along with the security pack
[08:16] Daniel Ortiz: A few red flags we've seen with other vendors: hidden egress fees, non-transparent fallback model behavior, and opaque logging. We need clear pricing and logs
[08:28] Avery Chen: Understood. We'll include a detailed pricing sheet with egress assumptions and outline fallback policies and logging levels in the security pack
[08:40] Marcus Lane: For the bench we'll include a test that exercises fallback under load so you can observe quality delta between primary and fallback models
[08:49] Rina Patel: One operational question: how are model rollouts handled? If a new model version has regressions can we rollback automatically?

[08:57] Marcus Lane: We support canary and A/B rollouts and automatic fallback rules. You can pin routes to model versions and set a default fallback model. Redwood Console shows rollout progress and regressions
[09:09] Elena Gomez: Great. On the pilot scheduling, I'll propose Nov 8 for kickoff with SRE plus a 1-week bench window. Can Redwood make Marcus and Avery available?
[09:18] Avery Chen: Yes, tentative yes. Marcus can lead the bench and I'll handle security and pricing follow-up
[09:25] Samir Kapoor: For bench access we'll need an ephemeral token exchange and audit trail of access — is that built in?
[09:33] Marcus Lane: We issue scoped API keys with adjustable TTL and can log token usage to your audit sink. We'll document the flow
[09:41] Rina Patel: Minor note — some transcripts earlier had model name mismatches; please include explicit model hashes or build ids in the bench report so we can trace results
[09:52] Marcus Lane: Good call, we'll include image IDs and model hashes in the report

[10:00] Avery Chen: Quick recap: Avery sends security pack + DPA + network diagrams by 2027-10-29; Marcus runs bench using Rina's prompt set and returns results by 2027-11-02; Elena to confirm pilot participants and date; Samir to share compliance checklist by 2027-10-31
[10:18] Elena Gomez: Sounds good — I'll confirm the Nov 8 slot and invite SRE and legal. Any blockers from Redwood's side?
[10:25] Marcus Lane: No blockers; just Rina's traffic profile and sanitized prompts and we'll be golden
[10:32] Daniel Ortiz: Great meeting. Thanks everyone, we'll look for the docs and bench next week
[10:39] Priya Nair: Thanks all — I'll open a shared runbook in the onboarding workspace and add owners
[10:45] Avery Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with attachments and a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff
[10:51] — meeting ended —
